scenes.anchor_text:
“Above silence, the illuminating storms—dying storms— illuminate the silence above.”
The above sample is noteworthy as it is a ketek, a complex form of holy Vorin poem.
scenes.scene_description: A vast, otherworldly storm rages in the sky above a desolate, rocky landscape. The storm's dying light weakly illuminates the alien terrain, hinting at a deeper, quieter darkness both above and below.

scenes.anchor_text: There is no record of this particular ketek in any repository of Vorin poetry, so it is very unlikely that the subject was merely repeating something he once heard. None of the ardents we showed it to had any knowledge of it,

scenes.anchor_text: We leave it to His Majesty’s mind, on a strong day, to puzzle out the meaning of why the storms might be important, and what the poem may mean by indicating that there is silence both above and below said storms.
